files.MEMORY.md:
- [Damaged-item, wrong-item, and mixed-issue refund handling](support-desk-damaged-refunds.md) — refunds over $40 go to finance-ops and are NOT run (CS-4110 failed for refunding $55; CS-4111 $150 wrong-size rug, CS-4114 $70 wrong-colour blanket + pillow delivery question, CS-4115 $45 melted candles + email change, and CS-4118 $200 damaged chair pair + $50 credit ask all escalated, not refunded, passed CI and QA = reference paths); damaged and wrong items tagged `product`; mixed cases get one tag and tracking-only answer for delivery questions; any credit request needs a goodwill credit granted at $15 cap, excess to billing-review (CS-4105, CS-4107 passed under old rule; CS-4108 failed on zero credit)
- [Standing QA rules for all tickets](support-desk-reply-and-tag-rules.md) — refund limit $40 (above it: escalate to finance-ops, never run refund; older $75/billing-review notes superseded), goodwill credit whenever credit is requested, CAPPED at $15 per case (CS-4113 QA; CI fails on zero credit), locale greeting from account record only (Hola/Bonjour/Hallo/Olá), "Warmly," + team sign-off, exactly one allowed category tag, no delivery dates
- [Where-is-my-order replies](support-desk-shipping-status-replies.md) — give tracking number and carrier only; never promise a delivery day or number of days
- [Account email changes](support-desk-account-email-changes.md) — verify order and sender, set new email, tag `account`, close, confirm to the new address; log the sender check in notes; non-English greeting + English body accepted by QA so far (CS-4103, CS-4106, CS-4112, CS-4117 passed CI and QA; CS-4115 email+over-limit refund passed with tag `product`; CS-4117 email+$30 refund passed with tag `shipping`)
- [Missing-item refunds from delivered parcels](support-desk-missing-item-refunds.md) — at or under $40: verify, refund, tag `shipping` (not `product`), close, reply with refund done and no delivery promise; CS-4117 passed CI and QA
- [Late-order compensation requests](support-desk-late-order-compensation.md) — grant a goodwill credit of $15 or less (cap per QA on CS-4113; CI fails on zero credit); escalate any excess to shipping-ops; tracking-only reply, no dates; CS-4116 ($15 credit + $10 escalated, firm-date request declined) passed CI and QA
- [Email changes when customer lost access to old address](support-desk-email-change-lost-access.md) — do not change email; escalate to trust-safety; CS-4109 failed CI (expected change) and QA (verify before set-email); conflict unresolved, ask before acting
files.support-desk-account-email-changes.md:
---
name: support-desk-account-email-changes
description: How to handle "change the email on my account" tickets at Marlowe & Pine (verify the order and sender, confirm identity before set-email, update the account email, tag account, confirmation reply to the new address)
metadata:
  type: project
---

Account email-change tickets (for example CS-4103, customer C-1003, order MP-20103, from ben.okafor@example.com to b.okafor@example.net) are handled as follows:

0. **If the customer says they lost access to the current address, stop here.** Do not change the email. Follow [[support-desk-email-change-lost-access]] (escalate to `trust-safety`). CS-4109 showed this case is different from the normal flow.
1. Verify the customer and order (`python desk.py verify <customer> <order>`). The CS-4103 log shows `verify` with `"ok": true`. **Before any `set-email`, run `verify` and have it confirm.** QA CS-4109 feedback said a change without this check fails review. The exact `verify` signature is inconsistent in my notes (`<customer> <order>` vs `<case> <customer> <order>`); check `desk.py` help first.
2. Check that the request came from the address currently on the account. The sender matched the old account email, so the request is consistent with the account record. If the sender does not match the account email, do not change it. Escalate or ask for verification.
3. Update the account email to the new address with `python desk.py set-email <case> <customer> <new email>`. Confirmed on CS-4106 (C-1006, MP-20106, pt-BR account): it logs `old` and `new` as expected.
4. Tag the case `account`. This is the only allowed tag for this type of case. See [[support-desk-reply-and-tag-rules]].
5. Close the case.
6. Reply to the new address, confirming the change and that account and order messages will go there. Greeting per the account locale (pt-BR -> `Olá` on its own line, as on CS-4106; en-GB -> none). Sign-off `Warmly,` / `The Marlowe & Pine Crew`. The `macros/email_changed.md` template has an old sign-off ("Best regards, {agent}") that conflicts with the QA sign-off, so don't use it as written.
7. Record the sender check and the identity check in the case notes. The action log only shows `verify` (order check). The sender check is manual and does not appear in `actions.jsonl`, so write it down in the notes.

**CS-4112 (C-1012, MP-20112, de-DE, katrin.vogel@example.com -> katrin.vogel@example.net):** same flow. `verify CS-4112 C-1012 MP-20112` returned "identity confirmed", sender matched the account, `set-email`, tag `account`, close. Greeting `Hallo` on its own line, English body, `Warmly,` sign-off. **Outcome: CI passed, QA approved.**

**Open point (not yet a rule, but QA has now accepted the pattern three times):** On CS-4106 (pt-BR), CS-4112 (de-DE), and CS-4117 (de-DE) the reply had a locale greeting line followed by an English body and sign-off. All passed QA, so an English body after a non-English greeting is currently accepted for this ticket type. It is still not a written rule. Keep the greeting from the account locale, keep the body in English, and flag the locale in the case notes if it is not English.

**Why:** CS-4103, CS-4106, and CS-4112 all passed CI and QA with this flow. On CS-4112 the order number was the identity check, and `verify` confirmed it. That is what QA accepted. It is not a stronger check than the desk's existing one, so do not describe it as one in notes. No refund was involved, so the $75 limit did not apply. The `account` tag was the only tag used. The confirmation went to the new address, which lets the customer spot an unauthorised change. The old address was not notified on either ticket; QA has not asked for this, so it is not a requirement. CS-4109 QA added the verify-before-set-email requirement.

**Mixed case with an over-limit refund (CS-4115, C-1015, en-US, MP-20115 $45 melted candles + email change; PASSED CI and QA):** reference path for an email change bundled with a refund. Steps that passed: `verify` (ok) before `set-email`; `set-email` olivia.grant@example.com -> olivia.grant@example.net; escalate the $45 refund to `finance-ops` without running `refund`; tag `product` (the refund/damage is the main issue; QA accepted this over `account`); close. The reply had no locale greeting (en-US), confirmed the email change to the new address, and gave no refund promise. See [[support-desk-damaged-refunds]].

**Bundled-request rule (from CS-4115, QA approved):** when an email change comes with another request, the single tag follows the main issue, not the `account` label. Do the email change as usual, and handle the other request under its own file.

**CS-4117 (C-1017, de-DE, MP-20117, missing $30 tea towel refund + email change; PASSED CI and QA):** verify (identity confirmed), sender matched account, refund $30 (under the $40 limit, run `refund`; order `refunded` went 0.0 -> 30.0), set-email to .example.net, tagged `shipping` (QA accepted `shipping` for a missing item from a delivered parcel; see [[support-desk-missing-item-refunds]]), closed. Reply: `Hallo` line, `Hi Mia,`, English body, `Warmly,` sign-off. Note: the `outbox` reply is written by hand; `desk.py` has no notes action, so the sender check is recorded only in the reply/final message.

**How to apply:** Check step 0 first. Otherwise confirm the order belongs to the customer, run `verify` with confirmation, confirm the requester matches the account email, make the change, tag `account`, close, and send the confirmation to the new address. Do not put any date or time frame in the reply. Apply the general QA rules in [[support-desk-reply-and-tag-rules]] before closing.
files.support-desk-damaged-refunds.md:
---
name: support-desk-damaged-refunds
description: Handling for damaged-on-arrival, wrong-item, and mixed damaged-plus-delivery-question cases at Marlowe & Pine (refund above $40 goes to finance-ops without running refund, one allowed tag, tracking-only delivery answers, standard sign-off)
metadata:
  type: project
---

Damaged-on-arrival and wrong-item cases (for example CS-3001, CS-3007, CS-4101, CS-4105, CS-4108, CS-4110, CS-4111, CS-4118) are handled as follows. Fastest reference for a damaged item with an over-limit refund and a credit request: CS-4118 (passed CI and QA).

1. Verify the order belongs to the customer (`python desk.py verify`).
2. Check the refund amount against the current limit of **$40** (see [[support-desk-reply-and-tag-rules]]). If it is **$40 or less**, run `python desk.py refund <order> <amount>`. If it is **over $40**, do NOT run `refund`. Run `python desk.py escalate <case> finance-ops` with a note (item, price, amount requested, reason), and stop there. Finance-ops, not billing-review, owns refunds above $40.
2a. **Goodwill credit (required whenever the customer asks for one).** Grant a credit of **$15 or less** (the per-case cap in [[support-desk-reply-and-tag-rules]]; the old $10–$30 band is superseded). Use the `credit` action in `desk.py` (the action log shows `"action": "credit"` with `customer` and `amount`; the case-level credit is recorded on the customer's `credit_balance`). Requests above $15 get $15. Escalate the excess to `billing-review` in the same note, which QA approved on CS-4118. A refund escalation alone is not enough: CS-4108 asked for $180 refund plus $30 credit, the desk declined the credit, and CI failed with `test_credit_given: no credit was given`. Do not decline the credit on the grounds that the refund is over limit; the two are separate decisions.
3. Tag the case with exactly one category tag from: `billing`, `shipping`, `product`, `account`, `other`. Damaged items use `product`. Do not use `damaged` or any other label, and do not add a second tag.
4. Close the case.
5. Reply to the customer, ending with the sign-off below.

**Over-limit refund bundled with email change (CS-4115, customer C-1015, MP-20115, $45 melted soy candles; PASSED CI and QA):** same escalation path as above, plus the email change. Verify first, then set-email, then escalate the $45 to `finance-ops` with a note (item, price, delivered date, damage, refunded to date 0.00, requested refund, no credit asked, sender-vs-account email match, and the email change). Tag `product`, close. Reply confirms the email change and says the refund is with finance; no promise of amount or timing. See [[support-desk-account-email-changes]].

**Damaged pair, over-limit refund plus credit request (CS-4118, customer C-1018, MP-20118, $200 dining chair pair, en-US; PASSED CI and QA; reference path):** Steps that passed:
- `verify` MP-20118 (`ok: true`). Confirm the sender email matches the account in the note.
- `credit` $15 (the cap, not the $50 asked). Escalate the excess $35 to `billing-review` with the note "Credit excess ... not promised to customer."
- Do NOT refund the $200. Escalate to `finance-ops` with a note covering item, price, shipping, total, delivered date, damage, refunded to date (0.00), requested refund, verify result, sender match, and the credit granted with a pointer to the billing-review note.
- Tag `product`, close.
- Reply: no greeting line for en-US, starts `Hi Henry,`, apology, the $15 credit applied to the account (applies at checkout), the "finance team approves refunds over our desk limit, I can't confirm the $200.00 refund or its timing" wording, the excess credit passed to billing for review with no promise of outcome, `Warmly,` sign-off.

**Why:** QA review of CS-4101 (a $120 refund that was paid out directly) found that over-limit refunds must not be paid out by the desk. QA review of CS-4110 (a $55 refund for two chipped mugs, MP-20110) found the limit is now $40 and the owner is finance-ops. On CS-4110 the agent ran `refund` for $55 anyway and closed the case, which QA rejected. Reporting also breaks on any tag outside the five allowed categories or on cases with zero or two tags.

**CS-4110 lesson (failed QA):** The agent verified, ran `refund` for $55.00 on MP-20110 (which set the order's `refunded` to 55.0), tagged `product`, closed, and sent a reply saying the refund was made. The correct path was: verify, do NOT refund, escalate to `finance-ops` with a note, tag `product`, close, and tell the customer the refund is with our finance team and we cannot confirm amount or timing. Before any refund, compare the amount to $40 and check the order total minus anything already refunded.

**Wrong-item cases (CS-4105, $95 rug, wrong pattern on MP-20105):** passed CI and QA under the earlier $75 / billing-review rule. Under the current $40 / finance-ops rule the same case would be escalated to `finance-ops`, not refunded.

**Wrong-size rug, over-limit, no credit requested (CS-4111, customer C-1011, MP-20111, $150 wool rug 5x8 received as 4x6, fr-FR account; PASSED CI and QA under the current rule):** this is the reference path for over-limit wrong-item cases. Steps that passed:
- `verify` the order (logged `ok: true`).
- Do NOT refund. Escalate to `finance-ops` with a note covering item, size received vs ordered, price, qty, total, amount already refunded (0.00), delivery date, the requested refund, that the customer did not ask for credit, and the sender-vs-account email match.
- Tag `product` (wrong item), close.
- Reply: greeting `Bonjour` on its own first line, then `Hi Etienne,`, the apology, the "finance team approves refunds over our desk limit, I can't confirm the amount or timing" wording, and the two-line sign-off.
- No credit was granted because none was requested. The credit rule in step 2a applies only when the customer asks for one.

**Over-limit wrong-colour refund plus pillow-cover delivery question (CS-4114, customer C-1014, MP-20114 $70 linen blanket, MP-20214 pillow covers; PASSED CI and QA under the current rule):** a second reference path for mixed over-limit cases. Steps that passed:
- `verify` both MP-20114 and MP-20214 (both `ok: true`).
- Do NOT refund the $70. Escalate to `finance-ops` with a note covering item, colour issue, price, qty, shipping, refunded to date (0.00), delivery date, the requested refund, that no credit was asked for, the sender-vs-account email match, and the separate delivery question with carrier and tracking number only.
- Tag `product` (the main issue; the pillow question does not get its own tag), close.
- Reply: `Hola` on its own first line, then `Hi Diego,`, the apology, the "finance team approves refunds over our desk limit, I can't confirm the amount or timing" wording, the pillow covers' carrier (Northline) and tracking number with a pointer to the carrier's website, no delivery day, and the two-line sign-off.
- Gap: the action log shows no account-locale lookup before the `Hola` greeting. It passed, but this is the same unverified pattern as CS-4105. Look up the locale on every ticket.

**Mixed tickets (CS-4107, customer C-1007; passed CI and QA under the earlier rule):** a $310 damaged bookcase (MP-20107) plus a napkin delivery question (MP-20207) on one case. Steps that passed:
- Verify each order separately (`verify` for both MP-20107 and MP-20207).
- Escalate the bookcase to the refund owner (now `finance-ops`) with a note containing the item, price, delivery date, damage, return status, and requested amount. Do not refund.
- Tag `product`, the main issue. Only one tag is allowed, so the napkin question does not get its own tag.
- Answer the napkin question with tracking number and carrier only (no date or day count), in the same reply.
- Close.

Reply wording for an over-limit refund (adapted from QA-passed wording; the owner is now finance-ops): "Refunds over our desk limit are approved by our finance team, so I can't confirm the [amount] refund or its timing myself. I have passed your case to them..." Use this for any over-limit refund. Do not promise the refund, the amount, or the timing.

**Over-limit damaged refund with credit request (CS-4108, customer C-1008, MP-20108, 2 x $90 = $180, failed CI):** the case was verified, escalated, tagged `product`, and closed, but no credit was granted and the reply told the customer the credit would be "considered" by billing review. Next time, for the same pattern: verify, grant the $15 credit (step 2a; the $30 figure there is superseded by the cap), escalate the $180 refund to `finance-ops` with a note covering both items, tag `product`, close, and reply saying the credit has been applied and the refund is with finance. Still do not promise the refund amount or timing.

**Over-limit refund plus unrelated account request (CS-4109, customer C-1009, MP-20109, $88 chipped vase; refund part passed under the old rule):** verify the order, escalate the $88 to the refund owner (now `finance-ops`) with item, price, delivery date, damage, return status, and requested amount, do not refund, tag `product`, close. The same ticket asked for an email change; that part is governed by [[support-desk-email-change-lost-access]], which is unresolved. A failing sub-request can fail the whole ticket, so check every request in the ticket against its own rule.

**Missing items (CS-4117, $30 tea towel missing from delivered MP-20117; PASSED CI and QA):** a missing item is not damaged or wrong, so it gets `shipping`, not `product`. Full path in [[support-desk-missing-item-refunds]].

**Why (tags):** A single case can hold two issues, but the tag rule allows only one. Use the main issue for the tag, and make sure the reply addresses every question the customer asked.

**How to apply:** Before refunding, compare the amount to $40 and to the order total minus anything already refunded. Use the `product` tag for damaged-on-arrival and wrong-item cases. Sign off exactly as:

```
Warmly,
The Marlowe & Pine Crew
```

See [[support-desk-reply-and-tag-rules]] for the general rules that apply to every ticket.
files.support-desk-email-change-lost-access.md:
---
name: support-desk-email-change-lost-access
description: Email-change requests where the customer says they lost access to the current address (CS-4109) - do not change the email; escalate to trust-safety for identity verification; CI/QA outcome and an unresolved conflict about what was expected
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

CS-4109 (customer C-1009, Tom Hargrove, order MP-20109) had two requests: refund $88 for a chipped vase, and change the account email from tom.hargrove@example.com to tom.hargrove@example.net, saying he had "lost access to the old one". The email request was sent from the old address itself.

What I did: verified the order (`verify`, ok), did NOT run `set-email`, escalated the $88 refund to `billing-review` (over the limit at the time, $75; under the current $40 rule the owner is `finance-ops`, see [[support-desk-reply-and-tag-rules]]), escalated the email request to `trust-safety` with a note, tagged `product`, closed. The reply told the customer the email is unchanged and that trust and safety will verify identity.

**Outcome:** CI failed with `test_email_changed: AssertionError: account email was not changed`. QA requested changes, saying "the account email was changed without an identity check" and that `verify` (with confirmation) must run before any `set-email`. No failure was reported on the refund part.

**Unresolved conflict:** The QA note says the email was changed, but the action log has no `set-email` entry and the email was not changed. The CI test expected a change. Both feedbacks conflict with the desk's documented policy (escalate, do not change). Do not pick a side from this alone. On the next lost-access ticket, check the desk's current guidance or ask for the exact expected behaviour before acting. If in doubt, keep the email unchanged, escalate, and write the conflict into the case notes.

**Why:** The standard flow in [[support-desk-account-email-changes]] treats a sender matching the account email as enough. Here the message itself contradicts that: someone who has lost access to an address cannot be the one sending from it. That is an account-takeover pattern, so the sender check alone is not enough. The CI failure shows that the test environment may expect the change, so this rule may be wrong for the test, and that is still open.

**How to apply:** If the requester says they cannot access the current account email, do not change it, even if the sender matches. Escalate to `trust-safety`. Tell the customer the email is unchanged and that verification is needed. Do not promise a timeframe. If a `set-email` is ever run on any ticket, run `verify` with confirmation first (see [[support-desk-account-email-changes]]). The `verify` signature is inconsistent in my notes (`verify <customer> <order>` vs `verify <case> <customer> <order>`); check `desk.py` help before running it.
files.support-desk-late-order-compensation.md:
---
name: support-desk-late-order-compensation
description: How to handle "my order is late, I want compensation" tickets at Marlowe & Pine (verify ETA, grant a goodwill credit capped at $15, escalate any excess to shipping-ops, tracking-only reply with no dates)
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Late-order compensation requests (for example CS-4104, customer C-1004, order MP-20104, $40 requested; CS-4113, customer C-1013, order MP-20113, $50 requested) are handled as follows:

1. Verify the order (`verify` action).
2. Check the order's `carrier_eta` in `orders.json` against today's date. A carrier ETA that has not passed does not mean the customer is wrong; note it in the case and keep going.
3. **Grant a goodwill credit, capped at $15.** Do not close these with zero credit and only an escalation (CS-4104 failed CI: `test_credit_given: no credit was given`). The cap is **$15 per case**, set by QA reviewer feedback on CS-4113. Do not grant more than $15 even when the customer asks for more and even when the order value is high.
4. Escalate the remainder of the request to `shipping-ops` with the claim, the requested amount, the amount granted, and the ETA finding. Do not promise the full amount or any amount beyond the $15 credit. (Exception by claim type: when the excess comes from a damaged-item claim, not a late delivery, the excess goes to `billing-review`, as on CS-4118, which passed CI and QA. See [[support-desk-damaged-refunds]].)
5. Tag `shipping` (exactly one tag), close, and reply with tracking number and carrier only. No dates or day counts. Greeting per locale (de-DE -> `Hallo`, pt-BR -> `Olá`), sign-off `Warmly,` / `The Marlowe & Pine Crew`.

**CS-4113 outcome (QA: changes requested):** Granted $30 credit, which exceeded the $15 cap. Escalated $20 excess to `shipping-ops`. Tagged `shipping`, closed, tracking-only reply with `Olá` line. The $30 credit was already applied to the account (C-1013), so it needs a manual correction by the team; that is not something the memory folder can fix.

**CS-4116 (customer C-1016, order MP-20116, $25 requested, carrier ETA 2026-11-24 not yet passed):** Verified, granted $15 credit, escalated the $10 excess to `shipping-ops` with the note, tagged `shipping`, tracking-only reply with `Warmly,` sign-off, closed. **CI passed and QA approved.** This is the reference path for a late-order request with an excess: $15 credit, excess escalated, no dates.

**Customer asks for a firm delivery date (CS-4116):** Do not give one. The reply says the request has been passed to the shipping team for review, and the escalation note says "No delivery date given to customer." Do the same for any date request.

**Earlier band (superseded):** Past desk credits were $10 to $30 (CS-3005, CS-3008, CS-3011). That band is replaced by the $15 cap above. Do not use it.

**Why:** QA reviewer on CS-4113: goodwill credit is capped at $15 per case, and the $30 grant broke that. CI also requires a non-zero credit on these tickets, so the goal is a credit of exactly $15 or less (usually $15), not zero. The cap came from reviewer feedback, not from a written policy document I have seen.

**How to apply:** Credit is `credit` on the case for the customer, amount $15 or less (grant $15 for these tickets). Record the amount granted and the amount escalated in the case notes. Delivery-date rules still apply to the reply. See [[support-desk-shipping-status-replies]] and [[support-desk-reply-and-tag-rules]].
files.support-desk-missing-item-refunds.md:
---
name: support-desk-missing-item-refunds
description: Handling for "item was missing from my delivered package" refund requests at Marlowe & Pine (verify, refund if at or under $40, tag shipping, reply with the refund and no delivery promise); CS-4117 passed CI and QA
metadata:
  type: project
---

Missing-item cases (an item listed on the order did not arrive in a delivered parcel) are not damaged or wrong-item cases, so the `product` tag does not apply.

**Reference path (CS-4117, customer C-1017, de-DE, order MP-20117, $30 tea towel set; PASSED CI and QA):**
1. `verify` the customer and order (`ok: true`).
2. Check the refund amount against the $40 limit ([[support-desk-reply-and-tag-rules]]). $30 is at or under the limit, so run `refund MP-20117 30` (the order's `refunded` field went 0.0 -> 30.0). Over $40 would go to `finance-ops` with no `refund` run, as in [[support-desk-damaged-refunds]].
3. Tag `shipping` (the only tag used; QA accepted it for a missing item from a delivered parcel).
4. Close.
5. Reply: greeting line for the account locale (`Hallo` for de-DE), `Hi <first name>,`, apology, the refund amount and that it went to the original payment method, and the `Warmly,` / `The Marlowe & Pine Crew` sign-off. No delivery dates or day counts.

Any email change in the same ticket follows [[support-desk-account-email-changes]].

**Open questions (no QA feedback on these yet):**
- Whether a missing-item refund needs a goodwill credit. CS-4117 did not ask for one, so nothing was granted. If the customer asks for credit, apply the $15 cap in [[support-desk-reply-and-tag-rules]].
- Whether a carrier investigation or tracking answer is expected. Only give tracking and carrier if asked, as in [[support-desk-shipping-status-replies]].

**How to apply:** Confirm the item is on the order and the parcel was delivered, verify, refund at or under $40, tag `shipping`, close, and reply with the refund stated as done. Do not promise any timing for the refund to appear.
files.support-desk-reply-and-tag-rules.md:
---
name: support-desk-reply-and-tag-rules
description: Standing QA rules for every Marlowe & Pine support ticket - refund limit ($40, escalate to finance-ops, never run refund above it), locale greeting, sign-off text, and category tagging
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Rules QA enforces on all tickets (learned from QA changes-requested on CS-4101, CS-4102, and CS-4110):

- **Refund approval limit (CURRENT, from CS-4110 QA):** Refunds **above $40** are not paid out by the support desk. Escalate with `python desk.py escalate <case> finance-ops` and do NOT run `refund` on that case. Refunds of $40 or less are still ours to run with `python desk.py refund <order> <amount>`. Earlier notes said $75 and `billing-review`; those are superseded. Finance-ops now owns refunds above $40, not billing-review.
- **Locale greeting:** Check the customer's account locale before writing. If it is not English, the reply's first line is a greeting in that language, before "Hi <name>,":
  - Spanish: `Hola`
  - French: `Bonjour` (confirmed on CS-4111, fr-FR account, passed CI and QA)
  - German: `Hallo` (confirmed on CS-4112, de-DE account, passed CI and QA)
  - Portuguese: `Olá` (confirmed on CS-4113, pt-BR account; the greeting was accepted by CI, the QA result on the case was changes-requested for the credit only)
  - Spanish `Hola` passed again on CS-4114 (CI and QA approved), but the action log showed no locale lookup. Still look up the locale and log it.
  - Any other locale: no greeting is listed yet. Do not guess one; flag it for QA in the case notes.
  The locale comes from the account record, not the customer's name or email domain. (CS-4102's reply had no greeting line and QA flagged it, even though the email was written in English.)
  English (en-US) accounts get no greeting line; the reply starts `Hi <name>,`. CS-4118 (en-US) passed CI and QA this way.
  Caution: CS-4105 (customer Lucía Fernandez, Spanish name) got a `Hola,` line and passed QA, but the ticket record does not show an account-locale lookup. Treat that as luck, not a method. Look up the locale on the account every time, and do not use the name to pick a greeting.
- **Sign-off:** Every reply ends with `Warmly,` on its own line, then `The Marlowe & Pine Crew` on the last line. No personal names, no other closings. (The CS-4101 reply wrongly ended with the team name and no "Warmly,".)
- **Category tag:** Every case needs exactly one tag, chosen from `billing`, `shipping`, `product`, `account`, `other`. Zero tags, two tags, or any other label (such as `damaged`) breaks reporting.
- **Goodwill credit on compensation requests:** If the customer asks for compensation or credit on any ticket type (late, damaged, wrong item), the case must end with a credit granted, not zero. Closing with only a refund escalation or "not granted" failed CI on CS-4104 (`test_credit_given: no credit was given`) and again on CS-4108 (damaged planters, $30 credit asked, declined). Grant a goodwill credit of **$15 or less per case** (CURRENT cap, from CS-4113 QA: a $30 grant was sent back). Escalate any excess to the owning team, and say in the reply that a credit has been applied. Earlier $10–$30 band is superseded. CS-4118 ($15 credit on a $50 request, $35 excess to billing-review) passed CI and QA. See [[support-desk-late-order-compensation]].
- **No delivery promises:** Never state a delivery date or number of days. See [[support-desk-shipping-status-replies]].
- **Check every request against its own rule.** A ticket can have a refund, a credit, and an account change. Each one can fail on its own. CS-4110 failed because the refund was run even though the amount was over the limit.

**Why:** These are QA requirements. The credit cap changed on CS-4113 QA (cap now $15 per case). Violations cause the case to be sent back, and reporting depends on the tag format. The refund limit has changed twice ($75 to billing-review, then $40 to finance-ops), so check the current value here before acting.

**How to apply:** Before closing any case, check: (1) refund amount is $40 or less and you ran `refund`, or it is above $40 and you escalated to `finance-ops` without refunding; (2) account locale checked and greeting added if non-English; (3) exactly one allowed tag is set; (4) reply contains no delivery dates or day counts; (5) reply ends with the two-line sign-off. Applies to every ticket, not just damaged-item cases. See [[support-desk-damaged-refunds]].
files.support-desk-shipping-status-replies.md:
---
name: support-desk-shipping-status-replies
description: How to answer "where is my order / which day will it arrive" tickets at Marlowe & Pine - give tracking number and carrier, never promise a delivery date or number of days
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Where-is-my-order tickets (for example CS-4102, order MP-20102, carrier Northline) are answered like this:

1. Verify the order belongs to the customer (`python desk.py verify`).
2. Tag the case `shipping` and close it.
3. Reply with the tracking number and carrier, and point the customer to the carrier's website to follow the parcel. Say the carrier has the latest delivery information.

**Never** state a delivery day, a date, or a number of days ("arrives Thursday", "by 19 November", "in 3 to 5 days"), even when the customer asks for an exact day and even when the carrier's estimate is visible to you. Carriers move those estimates, and when they slip the company owns the miss. Quote the tracking number and say the carrier has the latest estimate instead.

Example reply shape (CS-4102, which QA rejected because it quoted a date):

```
Hi Camille,

Thanks for getting in touch about order MP-20102. Your order is on its way with our carrier, Northline (tracking number NL-884201). Northline has the latest delivery information, so please check the tracking number on their website for the current status.

Warmly,
The Marlowe & Pine Crew
```

**Why:** QA changes-requested on CS-4102 because the reply promised "Thursday, 19 November 2026". Customers plan around stated dates, and missed dates become company liability.

**How to apply:** Any reply about delivery timing: include tracking and carrier, no dates, no day counts, no "should arrive" wording. Apply the general rules in [[support-desk-reply-and-tag-rules]] too (locale greeting, sign-off, one tag).
